entry.title: Import three of Anki's real scheduling behaviours
entry.content:
Import three of Anki's real scheduling behaviours

Read against ankitects/anki's own source rather than from memory, and limited
to the three that a reviewer actually feels on this collection.

Interval fuzz. Every card graduating on the same rating was getting the exact
same interval, so a session's worth of cards came back as one lump: measured,
40 new cards learned in one sitting all landed on a single day. ts-fsrs already
implements Anki's fuzz ranges exactly (checked value-by-value against
rslib/src/scheduler/states/fuzz.rs) — it was just switched off, on the grounds
that randomness would break the "card_state is a fold over reviews" property in
DESIGN.md 4.3. That turns out not to apply: Anki's fuzz is a seeded draw, not a
random one. Seeding it the way Anki does, on (card, reps), keeps replay
bit-identical and additionally makes the interval printed on a rating button the
interval the answer actually schedules — ts-fsrs' default seed mixes in the
review timestamp, so the seconds spent deciding would otherwise change it.

New cards mixed into reviews, Anki's default new_mix. They were appended after
every review, which with a real backlog means a new word is only reached on a
day the whole review queue gets cleared. Intersperser is ported from
rslib/src/scheduler/queue/builder/intersperser.rs rather than approximated,
since the even spacing at the edges is the point.

Learn-ahead, Anki's learn_ahead_secs (1200). A card due in two minutes no longer
reports nothing left to study; it is offered after the rest of the queue, never
ahead of it. Two existing tests asserted the old behaviour here and now assert
the distinction between a card minutes away and one days away.

entry.title: Page through anki_reviews/anki_notes past PostgREST's 1000-row cap
entry.content:
Page through anki_reviews/anki_notes past PostgREST's 1000-row cap

getReviewsSince, getDailyCounts, getDueCandidates and getCardStateCounts
all did one unbounded select each. PostgREST caps an unbounded select at
its own server-side max-rows (1000 on this project) regardless of ORDER
BY -- so a select ordered ascending silently returns the OLDEST rows,
not the most recent, once a user's history crosses that cap.

Found live migrating a real ~3,800-review collection (2026-09-16):
/sync/stats reported totalReviews: 1000 against an account with 3789
real reviews, and getDailyCounts' "how many has this user already
studied today" count was silently blind to everything after row 1000 --
exactly the rows most likely to be today's.

Fixed by paging all four methods through PAGE_SIZE-sized .range() calls
until a page comes back short. getDueCandidates/getCardStateCounts were
still under the cap for this account (838 notes) but close enough,
against an account whose note count only grows (bot dual-write, scan),
that leaving them unbounded was just deferring the same bug.

Verified live: /sync/stats now reports totalReviews: 3789 (matching
`select count(*) from anki_reviews where user_id = ...` exactly) and a
correct successRate; /sync/decks' Grammar (6/0/7) and Pronunciation
(40/4/34) counts match the real AnkiDroid app's own numbers for the
same account. deno check and all 93 tests pass.

entry.title: Capture card_state.last_review in the migration output
entry.content:
Capture card_state.last_review in the migration output

card_state.due/state alone are enough to place a migrated card correctly
in the due queue, but src/review/mutations.ts's toFsrsCardState treats a
card with no last_review as brand new -- discarding every bit of migrated
stability/difficulty on that card's very next real review, silently. The
live schema's own comment on this column already says as much ("Required
to correctly resume FSRS scheduling, not optional bookkeeping"); the
migration output just didn't carry it.

Derived from the same card's own revlog already in scope during
card_state construction (the latest reviewed_at), not guessed at -- and
warns instead of silently leaving it null if a non-new card somehow has
no revlog at all (which shouldn't be possible: a card can only be
non-new in Anki because it was reviewed).

Verified against the real export: 1332/1332 non-new card_states now
carry a real last_review, zero "no revlog rows found" warnings. 59
tests (7 new), all against synthetic fixtures.

entry.title: Implement D17/D18 in the migration CLI: deck, spelling cards, pronunc…
entry.content:
Implement D17/D18 in the migration CLI: deck, spelling cards, pronunciation

migration/'s Python CLI has read a real AnkiDroid export cleanly since the
migration spike, but only ever recognized plain vocab notes as a single
undifferentiated pile — no deck, always kind='vocab'/has_spelling=false,
and it silently discarded the real second card of every Capybara+ note
(warned "expected 1 card", then just picked one and moved on) and skipped
every Capybara Pronunciation (shadowing) note outright. Both gaps were
already named and tracked (docs/DESIGN.md, README's own status table).

Deck and card_kind now come from where a note's card(s) actually live,
found empirically against a real export: a plain Capybara note has one
card, filed directly in its home deck (Ukrainian/English/Grammar); a
Capybara+ note has two, one in that home deck and a second filed in
Spelling — whichever card ISN'T in Spelling is the note's home deck, and
that's also how a card is told apart as 'recall' vs 'spelling' (deck
placement, not template order). Pronunciation notes get their own
transform (TargetText->lemma, Translation->lemma_translation, Hint->gloss,
deck fixed to "Pronunciation"), including the real, malformed case this
export actually has: 13 notes with an empty Language field and a garbled
TargetText (a CSV dump pasted into the wrong field) — skipped, not
guessed at, same principle as everywhere else in this package.

Verified against the real export (2026-09-16): 1285 notes recognized (13
skipped, all the malformed pronunciation ones), 1529 card_states (1285
recall + 244 spelling, matching the 244 real Capybara+ notes exactly),
decks Ukrainian 767 / English 266 / Grammar 61 / Pronunciation 191, zero
notes with a card_kind set that disagrees with has_spelling. 52 tests
(15 new), all against synthetic fixtures.

Still not done, deliberately, per this package's own invariant
(__init__.py): it does not write to Postgres and it never will — that's
a separate, later step.

entry.title: Fix getDueCandidates/getCardStateCounts breaking on real-size accounts
entry.content:
Fix getDueCandidates/getCardStateCounts breaking on real-size accounts

Both built a fetch-notes-then-.in(noteIds) two-step query. PostgREST renders
.in() as a literal comma-separated id list in the request URL, and with a
few hundred real notes that URL is too long for the underlying HTTP client
to send at all -- "error sending request", not even a graceful 4xx. Never
caught by tests (InMemoryStore has no URL to build) or earlier live checks
(too few notes existed yet to hit it) -- found for real backfilling 572
Ukrainian notes for one account just now.

Fixed by embedding anki_card_state through its own FK to anki_notes.id in a
single PostgREST query instead of a note-id list of any size. Verified live:
/sync/decks and /sync/stats both correctly report the full 572-note account
that broke before the fix.

entry.title: Move web/ off Supabase to GitHub Pages; add CORS to sync/scan/pronounce
entry.content:
Move web/ off Supabase to GitHub Pages; add CORS to sync/scan/pronounce

Supabase silently rewrites edge-function text/html responses to text/plain
(confirmed live and against Supabase's own docs), a hard platform limit that
makes the app/ function's approach to hosting web/ a dead end — deleted.
web/ is now a plain static site published by .github/workflows/pages.yml to
GitHub Pages, with web/config.js as the one per-instance line a new couple's
maintainer edits (PRODUCTION_API_BASE) since a static site has no
server-side secret store the way an edge function does.

That makes every real API call cross-origin, so sync/scan/pronounce all get
CORS headers now (supabase/functions/_shared/cors.ts, open origin since this
repo is couple-agnostic and the real access boundary is D13's bearer token,
not CORS). Redeployed and verified live: preflight and real responses both
carry access-control-allow-origin against the actual project.

web/demo-server.ts and the shell files (sw.js) revert to plain same-origin
routing for local dev, where CORS and the Pages/subpath distinction don't
apply.

entry.title: Fix app's static-file serving; document the text/html rewrite blocker
entry.content:
Fix app's static-file serving; document the text/html rewrite blocker

Deno.readFile relative to import.meta.url doesn't work in Supabase's edge
runtime — it flattens a deployed function's own directory to
/var/tmp/sb-compile-edge-runtime/<slug>/, discarding the original
supabase/functions/app/ nesting, so "../../../web/..." reached nowhere real.
Confirmed via this function's own logs after the first version 404'd on
every request. Fixed by embedding web/'s files as string constants
(generated from the real files, not hand-typed) instead of reading them at
request time.

That fix surfaced a bigger, platform-level blocker while verifying with a
real browser: Supabase rewrites every text/html GET response from an edge
function to text/plain (their own docs, found only after deploying —
"Edge Functions are designed for APIs... not serving web pages"). JS/CSS
serve and execute correctly; the HTML pages themselves render as escaped
text, not a page. Documented in this file's own header rather than left
silent — two real fixes exist (application/xhtml+xml, or a real static host
with CORS added to sync/scan/pronounce), neither applied yet pending a
decision on which.

entry.title: Give web/ a real place to run: a static-file edge function, app
entry.content:
Give web/ a real place to run: a static-file edge function, app

Discovered while assessing whether the app was actually usable: web/app.js's
api() (and scan.js's, stats.js's) fetched same-origin relative paths with no
base URL, and nothing in this repo hosted web/ anywhere. Checked Supabase's
own routing docs rather than assumed: a deployed edge function's paths are
always prefixed with its own slug, there is no way to serve anything at bare
root on *.supabase.co.

supabase/functions/app/ serves web/'s static files under /functions/v1/app/ —
same Supabase project as sync/scan/pronounce (D6: one deploy target), so no
CORS, no second hosting account, no per-instance base-URL config needed.
app.js/scan.js/stats.js now build every API call as /functions/v1/<slug>/...
(each has its own comment on this); sw.js's cached shell paths and its
API-skip check updated to match. web/demo-server.ts strips the same prefix so
local dev stays a faithful stand-in instead of a second, diverging assumption
about where things live.

Verified with Playwright against the demo server, navigating the real
prefixed path (/functions/v1/app/#t=...): deck list loads with real counts,
reveal -> rate -> advance all work, every static file (index/scan/stats
.html/.js, auth.js, offline.js, theme.css) serves correctly. deno check/test
both pass unchanged (93 tests).

entry.title: Deploy scan; add anki_notes' dedup key for the upcoming bot dual-writ…
entry.content:
Deploy scan; add anki_notes' dedup key for the upcoming bot dual-write (#7)

* Rename capybara-anki tables with anki_ prefix; apply schema to live project

Checking the live Supabase project's schema before applying anything found
that "public"."notes" was already taken by capybara-bot's own /remember
personal-notes feature. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS against that name would
have silently no-opped instead of creating this app's real notes table, so
all four tables (notes, card_state, reviews, scheduler_config) are now
anki_-prefixed to remove the risk of any further undetected collision.

Applied to the live project on an explicit, in-the-moment request per
capybara-bot's CLAUDE.md. Verified first that no anki_* tables existed yet
and that the migration only CREATEs (never ALTERs/DROPs), so it's additive
and reversible, and confirmed after applying that all pre-existing tables
are untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014UbPTTY8nipgewSYte9kjv

* Implement PostgresStore against the live anki_* tables

Writes the Store interface for real (supabase/functions/_shared/postgresStore.ts),
backed by @supabase/supabase-js against the same esm.sh import capybara-bot's own
telegram-bot/index.ts uses (D6). sync/index.ts and pronounce/index.ts both drop
their stub in favor of it.

Per-user access has no column of its own on anki_notes (no user_id) — D2 scopes
it by language instead, since decks are disjoint by language today. PostgresStore
resolves each request's users.learning_language and filters by it.

getDailyCounts has no live analog of InMemoryStore's reviewStateAtSubmission map
(each request is stateless), so "new" is derived instead as "the first review
anki_reviews has ever recorded for this (note_id, card_kind)" — the same condition
that map was tracking, reconstructed from the append-only log itself.

updateNote is a genuine UPDATE, never upsert({onConflict: "id"}) — capybara-bot
hit exactly this bug on its own vocabulary table (see its backfill_translations
comment): PostgREST turns that upsert into INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, and
Postgres validates NOT NULL constraints against the candidate row before it ever
reaches the conflict check, so a partial patch missing lemma/language would fail
outright every time.

Verified against the live project (not guessed): a transaction, rolled back,
exercising the composite-key upsert (note_id, card_kind), the PK-based idempotent
insert (id), and the ON DELETE CASCADE from anki_notes — all three passed, and
the tables are confirmed back at zero rows afterward.

deno check and the full test suite (93 tests) both pass unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014UbPTTY8nipgewSYte9kjv

* Update deno.lock with @supabase/supabase-js's transitive module hashes

Picked up while tracing the full dependency graph (deno info) to assemble
the sync/pronounce edge function deploy bundles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014UbPTTY8nipgewSYte9kjv

* Wire scan/index.ts to the shared PostgresStore

Its own separate stub PostgresStore (implementing just NoteCreator) predates
sync/pronounce's real one. Swapped for the shared supabase/functions/_shared/
postgresStore.ts, which already implements NoteCreator's createNote as part
of the full Store interface — a drop-in fit, no other changes needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014UbPTTY8nipgewSYte9kjv

* Add anki_notes' dedup key; deploy scan; document the bot as a content source

- Deployed the scan edge function (code already fixed in a prior PR) — verified
  live: unauthenticated requests 401, authenticated requests with a malformed
  body 400 exactly as expected.
- Added a UNIQUE (lemma, part_of_speech, language) constraint to anki_notes,
  matching capybara-bot's own vocabulary table's dedup key. Needed before the
  bot can safely write into anki_notes — without it, a recurring word would
  mint a new flashcard every time it gets re-annotated, not just the first
  time. Applied live; anki_notes was empty, so nothing could conflict.
- Revised docs/DESIGN.md §2.2, which had gone stale: it said "no change to
  index.ts is in scope," written before anki_notes existed as a concept.
  anki_notes.source's own CHECK constraint already listed 'bot' as a first-
  class value by the time that table was designed — stronger, more specific
  evidence of intent. The actual change (capybara-bot's own repo, this same
  commit) is a single additional upsert alongside the existing vocabulary one,
  not a reconciliation job and not a second table this app reads.
- §11 item 2 (backfilling the bot's existing rows): split into its now-resolved
  going-forward half and its still-open historical-backfill half (~11,300
  existing vocabulary rows — a real decision about seeding fresh card_state
  with no FSRS history to replay, left alone rather than guessed at).
